cells.tense: You are letting a feeling settle on its own without freezing it in place.
cells.ask: Sit with one feeling today without explaining or fixing it, and when the sitting is done, let that be the whole of it.
cells.core:
You feel something and you don't hurry it. Nothing is pushed down and nothing leaks out sideways, it lands, it settles, and you stay close enough to know what it is. There is a floor under that kind of attention, which is why people can be honest near you without being handled.

Most people either dump a feeling or bury it, and you can sit in the middle of one and adjust as it moves. The invitation is to let an idea go deeper than a feeling usually gets to, past the point where you think you know what it means, and give the pattern underneath some room. What you do with that is yours. Nothing here needs a decision today.
cells.sheetLine: You let feeling settle without burying it.
cells.verb: letting feeling settle until it can be sat with
cells.place: the ongoing adjustment that keeps a flow steady

cells.tense: You are guarding a version of how this should feel before it has had room to happen.
cells.ask: Let one thing end before you decide what it meant; write what actually happened, without the lesson, and leave it there.
cells.core:
You are trying to keep a connection safe by holding it at a certain temperature. Ahead of you sits a picture of how this should feel, and you spend present energy making things match it, which means you are not quite here for what is actually on offer.

The vigilance is not cruelty. It is care that has run ahead of its own patience. Feelings do not stay steady because someone watches them, and the watching costs you the ease you are trying to protect. What grows here gets gathered later, not now. Let something wind down without managing the ending, then look at what it produced instead of what you hoped.

cells.tense: You slipped out of something you felt and you are still standing there waiting on a signal that already came.
cells.ask: Put one feeling and one thing you will do about it in a single written sentence, then read it out loud once.
cells.core:
You can feel what is yours, and you bring less of it out than you carry. The footstep back happened at some point, and it turned into a way of keeping your footing that still runs, even where it no longer fits.

Sitting steady inside a feeling is not gone. It went quiet, and quiet looks like calm from the outside. What is missing is the small interior work of gathering what you notice into something you can act from. Nothing gets balanced when nothing is brought to the table. One sentence, said once, brings something forward. That is the whole of today's work.

cells.tense: You are already adjusting how close things get, and you talk as if that were just how it is.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about your own state out loud, framed as yours, with no story and no lesson attached.
cells.core:
You are already doing the work of staying steady inside a connection, noticing the pull, adjusting how much you show, keeping the temperature even. From where you stand it looks like the situation is simply like that, and you are only responding to it.

The part that gets no credit is yours. You choose how close to stand, and you have been calling that choice the situation. Bring the thinking back to something simpler and check it: what do you understand here, right now, before building any theory about it. The adjustment holds either way. The only thing added today is saying that it is you doing it.
cells.sheetLine: You are holding the balance and you call it the situation.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is the location of the old door in the Too Little cell: a wound is implied that the record never states. The reader could rightly say, 'I was never excluded,' and I have no material for what happened, so that cell's one clause about a door must not name who closed it, how long ago, or what it cost. The asks survive being wrong — each is one visible act, and a person who disagrees with the read can still do it and learn something from the result. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the Too Much sheetLine, which would only flatter someone's own story of being generous with attention.
